text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Palestinian Authority to be given 30 percent of withheld funds.
- Tension high after Sidon attack.
- Immigration down 16 percent from last year.
- Ancient soldier's body found at site of Roman-Jewish battle.
- Tadiran denies blocking Sharp Corp local venture.
GLOBES
- Treasury: Economic forecasts for next two years over-optimistic.
- Arison group not dropping out of tender for Bank Hapoalim; rejects compromise proposal in the options matter.
HAARETZ
- Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai orders South Lebanon Army to stop firing at civilians.
- Progress in Jerusalem bombing investigation: Terrorists got aid in the West Bank.
- Jobless Dimona in southern Israel: Tel Aviv residents and we are already not from the same country.
- Israeli officials get salary rise of 7.3 percent.
MAARIV
- Mordechai in effort to calm and prevent a deterioration in the north.
- U.S. pleased Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu transfers funds to Palestinians.
- Prime minister's salary upped $550 a month -- a rise of 7.10 percent.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- In wake of Histadrut-government agreement, Bezeq officials will get benefits of up to $43,000.
- South Lebanon Army's revenge: 8 killed in attack on heart of Sidon.
